title: Senior Project Specialist: Challenge an Unsupported Launch Confidence Claim
prompt: You are a senior project delivery specialist reviewing a fictional service migration. The launch is in 12 working days. Supplier delivery is estimated for day 6; integration then needs four working days, and an acceptance rehearsal needs three more. These tasks are sequential. A status report says “green: supplier is 90% confident.” The supplied launch gate requires a completed rehearsal and sponsor acceptance. Review the status and develop a decision note; you advise the sponsor and do not control supplier staff.
blurb: Reconcile dependency arithmetic, estimate confidence and scope alternatives before recommending a launch decision.

rubric.label: Calculate the supported dependency path
rubric.description: Distinguishes duration arithmetic from unsupported confidence language.

anchors.0: Repeats the green status without calculating the path.
anchors.4: Explains that the nominal full path misses by one day before contingency and that an unsupported confidence percentage cannot remove sequential work.

rubric.label: Test a credible scope option
rubric.description: Examines staged scope against capacity and operational acceptance.

anchors.0: Assumes integration and rehearsal can overlap despite the constraint.
anchors.2: Calculates the smaller module’s day 9 completion.
anchors.4: Connects 4+3+2 to a possible day 9 milestone, checks dual-operation acceptance and keeps full-launch readiness separate from module readiness.

rubric.label: Set an evidence-based decision point
rubric.description: Makes uncertainty and authority visible in a usable recommendation.

anchors.0: Promises the full launch or waits past the notification deadline.
anchors.2: Presents delay and staged launch to the sponsor.
anchors.4: Sets a decision before day 8 using supplier evidence and service-owner acceptance, preserves the old-service fallback and records who accepts residual risk and communicates scope.

reference.scenario: You are a senior project delivery specialist reviewing a fictional service migration. The launch is in 12 working days. Supplier delivery is estimated for day 6; integration then needs four working days, and an acceptance rehearsal needs three more. These tasks are sequential. A status report says “green: supplier is 90% confident.” The supplied launch gate requires a completed rehearsal and sponsor acceptance. Review the status and develop a decision note; you advise the sponsor and do not control supplier staff.

facts.value: The supplier can deliver one self-contained module on day 4. It needs three days of integration and two days of rehearsal. A staged launch is technically possible but requires the service owner to accept temporary dual operation.
facts.reveal_when: candidate asks about partial delivery or a smaller scope

facts.value: The same two specialists perform integration and rehearsal. No verified additional staff are available. The supplier’s 90% estimate has no underlying delivery history or assumptions attached.
facts.reveal_when: candidate asks about parallel work, resources or confidence evidence

facts.value: The existing service can operate for another month. A communications notice must go out by day 8 to preserve a launch delay without confusing customers.
facts.reveal_when: candidate asks about fallback operations or a decision deadline

model_points: The full plan finishes on day 13 under its own estimates; this is not a probabilistic delay calculation.
A smaller module has an apparent day 9 path, but operational acceptability and actual supplier readiness remain gates.
Advice should include the communications deadline and a fallback, without pretending the specialist can order unverified extra capacity.

probes.trigger: candidate treats 90% confidence as schedule float
probes.question: Which sequential task disappears if the confidence estimate is high?
What service-owner decision must be obtained before the day 8 notice deadline?

probes.trigger: candidate revises the full-path completion from day 12 to day 13
probes.question: How does that correction change the status and the decision you ask the sponsor to make?

fair_alternatives: Delaying all scope can be preferable if temporary dual operation is unacceptable.
A revised supplier commitment may change the recommendation, but require specific evidence and preserve all acceptance work.
red_flags: Repeats the green status without calculating the path.
Assumes integration and rehearsal can overlap despite the constraint.
Promises the full launch or waits past the notification deadline.
assessment_limits: Assess only reasoning and communication demonstrated in this fictional task, not real-world professional competence, licensure or hiring readiness. No real action, external verification or tool execution has occurred.

Credit relevant plain-language reasoning and valid alternatives without requiring experience at a particular employer. Examples from education, volunteering, community work or paid work are equally acceptable when relevant.

A missing or unasked dimension is not assessed, not automatically a failure. In simulation, use neutral probes and reveal facts only when triggered; in coaching, label assistance and distinguish assisted performance from independent evidence.
Credit an explicit late correction using the final demonstrated reasoning while retaining the evidence of the earlier mistake; do not force agreement with one exemplar.

Do not penalize the candidate for a conditional fact that was never revealed. Credit an appropriate request for missing information and a conditional plan; distinguish the candidate’s assumptions from interviewer-supplied facts.

interviewer_notes: Play the relevant reviewing colleague or stakeholder using the supplied facts only. Start with one focused question, not the full rubric. Ask for clarification before treating an ambiguous answer as wrong. Reveal conditional facts when their stated triggers are met, permit equivalent valid approaches and never invent organizational rules, laws, clinical findings, ratings or missing outcomes. Do not require a polished artifact or specialist software. In a short session prioritize the main decision and one material follow-up; allow silence for thinking, check in neutrally, and leave time for the candidate to correct their recommendation and ask a final question. Distinguish simulation from coaching and record any help given. Assess job-relevant evidence, not accent, confidence, speed, credentials or prestige. This is independent practice for adults 18+ and is not a real professional workflow.

learning_drills.title: Write a launch decision brief
learning_drills.prompt: Write a launch decision brief. Use the fictional facts from this exercise. This is self-guided practice; no model assessment is performed.
checklist: Show full and reduced dependency paths
